verification.note: Reproduced by reading the code. refine.py:318 imports _build_chunks_from_words from app.workers.whisper, refine.py:353 calls it, refine.py:378 deletes the Embedding rows and refine.py:380 deletes the TranscriptChunk rows for the file, then refine.py:386 re-inserts them. whisper.py:1375 defines _persist_transcript, which calls _build_chunks_from_words at whisper.py:1398. subtitle_builder.py:575-577 (build_vtt) renders through build_cues. Every direct caller of is_digit_separator/splits_number (subtitle_builder.py:247, 355, 480, 502, 510, 526, 531 and whisper.py:634) sits inside a function the touch-point list names. The touch-point list does leave out refine.py and _persist_transcript. The spec body does cover the behaviour, though: docs/specs/digit-colon-times.md:71-72 says chunks written by a transcription or refine run may end at different words, and :99 says chunk boundaries of refined text move. So the gap is in the touch-point list only, not in the spec. digit_separator.py:5 already contains ':' and '：' in _SEPARATORS, so these transitive paths do get the new behaviour.

specification_compliance: digit_separator.py:5 adds ':' and '：' to _SEPARATORS. The digit set stays 0-9, as the spec states for full-width digits.
Spec §4 and §9 (digit-colon-times.md:71-72, :99) already cover the refine re-chunk path that R1-TP-1 says is missing from the touch points.
regression_risks: Refine re-chunking (refine.py:353-386) deletes and rewrites chunks and their embeddings, so after this change a refined file's chunk boundaries can differ around colon times. The spec documents and accepts this.
